Overview 
---

`badlm` is a small R package for inferring the temporally delayed dependence
between a predictor and a response variable. It fits the Bayesian adaptive
distributed lag model described in

  - Rushworth, A. _Bayesian adaptive distributed lag models._ (2018). [arXiv:1801.06670.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.06670)

The lag curve is represented by a B-spline basis whose coefficients receive a
first-difference penalty with lag-varying precision. The log precisions are
themselves smoothed by a random walk prior, so the amount of smoothing adapts
to the shape of the lag curve and the maximum lag can be chosen generously
without overfitting. A copy of the paper source is kept in the `paper/`
directory of this repository.

Installation 
---

To install the development version of the package, use
```{r, eval = FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=F}
devtools::install_github("alastairrushworth/badlm")

# load the package
library(badlm)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=F}
library(badlm)
set.seed(2018)
```


`badlm` example
---


Generate a distributed lag function
```{r lagfun, cache = FALSE}
# a nice distributed lag function - hump
x          <- 0:50
dlfunction <- -0.1 + (0.01*exp(-0.2*x) + exp(dnorm(x, sd = 4, mean = 10))) / 10

plot(x, dlfunction, type = "l")
```

Generate predictor and response under the distributed lag function
```{r simulate, cache = FALSE}
# exposure is an AR(1) process
expose        <- arima.sim(model = list(ar = 0.5), n = 500, sd = 0.1)
expose        <- (expose - mean(expose)) / sd(expose)
lag_mat       <- lag_matrix(expose, p = 50)
deaths.sig    <- lag_mat %*% dlfunction
deaths        <- deaths.sig + rnorm(450, sd = 0.01)
```

Try to recover the distributed lag function. The first half of the iterations
is discarded as burn-in by default; Metropolis proposals are tuned only during
that period.
```{r fit, cache = FALSE, results='hide'}
dlm_est <- badlm(x = expose, y = deaths, 
           nlag = 50, k = 30, samples = 10000)
```

The fitted object holds pointwise posterior summaries of the lag curve, the
posterior draws of the curve itself, and draws of the effective degrees of
freedom of the fit.
```{r summary}
head(dlm_est$coefs)
mean(dlm_est$ed)
```

Plot the resulting lag curve

```{r lagcurve}
plot_lagcurve(dlm_est)
```
